solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prediction is a warning, of course, to players

parts.note: on a golf course 'Fore!' is the shouted warning to people in the ball's path
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A forecaster tells a team of performers that their forecast is a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to the golf course: FORE is the golfer's warning cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what is expected to happen, such as tomorrow's weather, so a synonym for prediction.

clue.text: Hitch up and hike to Barking with tent

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of the words around it are sent crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: A camper fastens up gear and treks off to Barking, a district of east London, carrying a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the London place name but is the anagram signal working on HIKETO and TENT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hitched is informal for marrying, and the idiom for wedding is to tie the knot.

clue.text: Revolutionary dullard such as could be pickled

parts.note: a Red is a revolutionary communist
a cabbage is informal for a dull, inactive person

explanation.surface: A radical who is a bore might, the clue jokes, deserve to be preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple brassica is commonly preserved in vinegar as a pickle, so it is an example of something picklable.

clue.text: With head fully depressed trick one who manipulates selfishly

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for trick is pushed right down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: Someone pushes another's head down in a dirty trick, the act of an exploiter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the head is the top letter; 'fully depressed' sends R from the start of RUSE to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exploits others for personal gain is called a user.

clue.text: Top on head of Mafia

definitions.meaning: the top man, the boss: from the Italian for head
the leader of a Mafia crime family has this title

explanation.surface: The man at the top sits at the head of the Mafia.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'head', the title is used for a mob boss, the top man of a crime family.

clue.text: Lyrics regularly maintained by toddlers

indicators.note: every other letter of the following word is kept, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Nursery rhymes are routinely kept up by small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject, odes are a classic form of lyric verse.

clue.text: Go near rotten fruit

indicators.note: rotten describes something spoiled and broken down, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Don't approach decaying produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit is a standard example of a fruit.

clue.text: Chap with cool top

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
to ice is to chill or cool

explanation.surface: A man wearing a stylish shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper part of a dress or a close-fitting garment, a kind of top.

clue.text: Normal colour of an upright tree

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means usual or ordinary
a regiment's colours are its flag
a tree or shrub grown on a single tall erect stem

explanation.surface: It reads like a gardener asking about the usual hue of an erect tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means typical, a flag carried into battle, and a fruit tree trained on one upright stem.

clue.text: I let go legionnaire's cap with tons being carried

indicators.note: the letter I is released and replaced in the cap's name

parts.note: a kepi is the flat-topped peaked cap worn by the French Foreign Legion

explanation.surface: A soldier confesses to dropping his cap while lugging heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tons' supplies T in place of the released I.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods a shop kept are ones it carried in stock, so the past tense of retaining or holding.

clue.text: British on getting into vehicle slump, it may save the planet

indicators.note: the letters for British and on are put inside the pair of words for vehicle and slump

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to sink is to slump or drop

explanation.surface: A Brit flops into a car, which hardly sounds like something that helps the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Forests and oceans absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide, helping to limit global warming and protect Earth.

clue.text: Female with outstanding presence

parts.note: ace means excellent or outstanding

explanation.surface: A woman with a remarkable charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the face of someone is to be in their presence, and a face can mean someone appearing, as in a familiar face.

clue.text: Good for Porthos beginning to kick something large in novel

parts.note: Porthos is one of Dumas's French Three Musketeers, and French for good is bon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a buster is informal for something unusually big, as in a blockbuster

explanation.surface: A musketeer's taste for a large kick in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A racy, steamy popular novel full of sex scenes is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Focus on heart of bias in old Nilote country

parts.note: the nub is the central point or crux of a matter

indicators.note: the central letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: Concentrate on the core of prejudice in an ancient African state.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient region along the Nile in present-day Sudan was home to Nilotic peoples.

clue.text: Where to poll harmonious quartet

definitions.meaning: to poll is an old word for cutting hair, done at a hairdresser's for men
an unaccompanied four-part close-harmony vocal group

explanation.surface: It reads as a question of where to hold a vote, and a singing group.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a men's hairdressing shop and a style of close-harmony singing by four voices.

clue.text: Schism in a seaport being settled

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged until they settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A split in a port town while people are being resettled.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division between groups, and the answer is the act of splitting apart.

clue.text: Knock out second beer barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for beer or wine

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a second barrel of beer and is flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: To render someone senseless with a blow is to daze them, the same idea as a knockout.

clue.text: Feature of corner about to disappear, making light of caution

indicators.note: the letter for about vanishes from the road word

parts.note: the camber is the slope of a road surface, built into bends
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A driver loses the bank on a bend, about to vanish, while the warning lamp shows.
explanation.definitionFit: In traffic signals the middle lamp, between red and green, warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Settled up quietly with help

parts.note: P, from the musical piano, means quietly
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone cleared a debt discreetly, with assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle up a bill is to hand over the money owed, so the past tense of paying.

clue.text: Setter in anagrams to excite curiosity

indicators.note: the clue names its own device: the words before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker puts anagrams in to intrigue solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword-convention I or ME, but both words are taken as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue or arouse attention in someone is to make them curious.

clue.text: In leather gal shocked

indicators.note: shocked suggests a jolt that scrambles the letters before it

explanation.surface: A woman in leather clothing is scandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a preposition but is the definition: fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable, and the idiom for a passing craze is the same.

clue.text: Gosh! Muggins put up a scrubber

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: muggins is British slang for a fool or gullible person, often oneself
ah is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as a dupe sets up a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous pod of a gourd is used as a bath sponge for scrubbing skin.

clue.text: Blast it! Lead's overturned

indicators.note: the word is turned over so it reads backwards

parts.note: the lead is the star of a show, with the 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone swears as the dog's lead or the leading role is upended.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of annoyance, like Damn! or Drat!

clue.text: Sarge pours out an expression of disdain

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A sergeant gives vent to his contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: From Aesop's fox, the idiom describes disparaging what one cannot have, a disdainful attitude.

clue.text: Hives in tree below river

indicators.note: in a down entry the tree's word sits under the river's letter

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Bee colonies in a tree beneath a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives' looks like beehives, but it is the skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives, or urticaria, is an itchy red skin eruption, a kind of skin outbreak.

clue.text: Irish broadcaster getting round a cost

indicators.note: the broadcaster's letters go around the a

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national public broadcaster

explanation.surface: An Irish TV network gets round a budget problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a charge or price for something, such as an hourly fee.

clue.text: Look! Stock up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a shop that will keep an item stocks it

explanation.surface: Look, the inventory has risen!
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance is a peek, used as an imperative to glance at something.

clue.text: Sharp quiff

definitions.meaning: quiff is old British slang for a loose woman

explanation.surface: It reads as a stylish, pointed hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means acidic in taste and is also slang for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Musical recorder put in class?

indicators.note: the word for put goes inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: It asks whether a recorder, the woodwind, was introduced into a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' suggests the woodwind instrument, but it is a tape that records music.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact cassette is a tape cartridge on which music is recorded and played back.

clue.text: Old boy to 'eave up performer

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to heave up is to hoist; in dropped-aitch Cockney it becomes 'oist

explanation.surface: A Cockney old boy is told to lift a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eave shows a dropped H, so hoist loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe is an instrumental musician, a kind of performer.
